nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a subspace of $E$, and let $x \in E$ lie outside the topological closure of $S$. Then some continuous linear functional $f$ in the topological annihilator of $S$ satisfies $f(x) = 1$.
nodes.title: Separation, normalized

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a subspace of $E$, and let $x \in E$ lie outside the topological closure of $S$. Then some continuous linear functional $f$ in the topological annihilator of $S$ satisfies $f(x) \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Separation

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Every subspace $S$ of $E$ is contained in the topological coannihilator of the topological annihilator of $S$.
nodes.title: A subspace lies in its double annihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a subspace of $E$, and let $f : E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional. Then $f$ lies in the topological annihilator of $S$ if and only if $f(x) = 0$ for every $x \in S$.
nodes.title: Membership in the topological annihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\Phi$ be a subspace of the continuous dual of $E$, and let $x \in E$. Then $x$ lies in the topological coannihilator of $\Phi$ if and only if $f(x) = 0$ for every $f \in \Phi$.
nodes.title: Membership in the topological coannihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S \subseteq T$ be subspaces of $E$. Then the topological annihilator of $T$ is contained in the topological annihilator of $S$.
nodes.title: The topological annihilator reverses inclusion

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The topological annihilator of the zero subspace of $E$ is the whole continuous dual of $E$.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator of the zero subspace

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be a subspace of $E$. The topological annihilator of $S$ is the zero subspace of the continuous dual of $E$ if and only if $S$ is dense in $E$.
nodes.title: Density criterion via the annihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ and $T$ be subspaces of $E$. Then $S$ and $T$ have the same topological annihilator if and only if they have the same topological closure.
nodes.title: The annihilator determines the closure

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ and $T$ be subspaces of $E$. The topological annihilator of $S + T$ is the intersection of the topological annihilators of $S$ and $T$.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator of a sum of subspaces

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological annihilator of $E$, viewed as a subspace of itself, is the zero subspace of $E^*$: a continuous linear functional vanishing everywhere on $E$ is zero.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator of the whole space

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every subspace $S$ of $E$, the topological annihilator of the topological closure $\overline{S}$ equals the topological annihilator of $S$: a continuous linear functional vanishing on $S$ vanishes on $\overline{S}$.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator of the closure

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $S$ be a subspace of $E$. The topological coannihilator of the topological annihilator of $S$, that is, the subspace of vectors of $E$ killed by every continuous linear functional vanishing on $S$, is the topological closure of $S$.
nodes.title: Bipolar theorem

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological annihilator of a subspace $S$ of $E$ is the subspace of $E^*$ consisting of the continuous linear functionals $f$ with $f(x) = 0$ for all $x \in S$.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. If $\Phi \subseteq \Psi$ are subspaces of $E^*$, then the topological coannihilator of $\Psi$ is contained in the topological coannihilator of $\Phi$.
nodes.title: The topological coannihilator is antitone

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological coannihilator of the zero subspace of $E^*$ is all of $E$.
nodes.title: Topological coannihilator of the zero subspace

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. For subspaces $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ of $E^*$, the topological coannihilator of their supremum $\Phi + \Psi$ is the intersection of the topological coannihilators of $\Phi$ and $\Psi$.
nodes.title: Topological coannihilator of a sum of subspaces

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological coannihilator of $E^*$ itself is the zero subspace of $E$: a vector killed by every continuous linear functional is zero.
nodes.title: Topological coannihilator of the whole dual

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological coannihilator of a subspace $\Phi$ of $E^*$ is the subspace of $E$ consisting of the vectors $x$ with $f(x) = 0$ for all $f \in \Phi$.
nodes.title: Topological coannihilator

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
